direction.premise: An identity-detection instrument for Marvel Rivals: instead of a superhero personality quiz, the player reads their own combat style like a classified tactical dossier.
direction.composition: The phone opens with a large numbered crosshair insignia and one primary action; questions become full-height field notes with a single high-contrast answer cluster. Results unfold as a ranked case-file with a prominent inked hero monogram plate, skill signature and ten numbered strips.
direction.shapeLanguage: Severed corner cuts, fine survey grid, wide horizontal strike lines, numbered roster stamps and abstract insignias derived from actual hero initials.
direction.surfaceAndMaterial: Matte pale mineral paper and deep forest-green ink, subtle halftone stripes, opaque tactical olive overlays. No neon, no glass, no borrowed movie stills.
direction.paletteLogic: Ivory ground and evergreen primary ink; pale sage records selections and data; muted apricot differentiates duelists; every color used to encode a real interaction or role.
direction.typography: Condensed industrial display for heroic titles, compact monospaced dossier serials and direct readable Arial for answers.
direction.signature: A colored tactical encounter diagram with ally/enemy positioning interrupts the question flow; decisions change the latent fingerprint and reveal a real ranked roster.
direction.distinction: Unlike rivals-fit-lab's dual-ended psychometric questionnaire and blue typography, RIVALS DNA uses contextual four-option choices and arena decision diagrams with a separate ease-vs-enjoyment ranking. Unlike rivals-roulette's random spinning pick, the list always follows explicit player answers.

architecture.primaryVerb: Choose how you actually want to fight across twenty context-rich questions, then inspect ranked hero dossiers and rate what worked in matches.
architecture.physicalFeedback: The selected answer inks over immediately; progress advances to the next numbered file. Opening a ranked hero lifts a dense performance dossier with separate score and feedback controls.
architecture.spatialRationale: The active question or tactical diagram takes the top half while four full-width tactile options fill the phone's reachable area. Rankings are a scrollable reading collection, not a fake single-screen game.

comparisons.spatialDifference: RIVALS DNA presents field-case-choice panels with one numbered question at a time; rivals-fit-lab uses a different survey reading structure.
comparisons.interactionDifference: This app asks live tactical-choice situations and collects post-match votes that update the ranking rather than only continuous paired scales.

comparisons.spatialDifference: RIVALS DNA is a matte archival instrument with dense dossier strips, not a large center wheel and random selection stage.
comparisons.interactionDifference: This app calculates stable fitted rankings and role-complementary pairs rather than spinning or banning random heroes.

production.renderer: App-owned static semantic DOM with embedded authored SVG battlefield diagrams and bespoke abstract initial-based hero insignias; no remote image dependency.
production.focalAsset: A custom crosshair/fingerprint vector icon and distinct angled rectangular sigils generated from each known hero name.

motion.character: Fast pressed answer response and slight tactile displacement; category progress advances without animation debt.
motion.action: Select one battle response or set a difficulty slider.
motion.anticipation: Unselected paper buttons have outlined index slots and suggest an immediate direct choice.
motion.response: Choice turns sage, check mark and saved score appear immediately, next action unlocks.
motion.followThrough: A new numbered case file replaces the old one; results unfold into a ranked file on completion.
motion.interruption: Rapid repeated inputs update one answer; every state persists before moving; pressing back restores the selected answer.
motion.reducedMotion: All CSS transitions and animation disappear while selection and progress remain readable.

evidence.expectedChange: The first of 20 questions appears with selectable tactical preferences.
